Summary: Hebrews' prisoner command: remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them, and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body.
Commandment: Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body.
Application: Remembrance here is identification: bound with them, as if in the same body. It is the prison-visiting command in its most inward form — sympathy that puts itself in the cell.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: 'as bound with them' and 'as being yourselves also in the body' (Hebrews 13:3).
